executiveSummary: GM0432's official 2025 identity, contained centre, 12,491 residents, 46 neighbourhoods, five BAG places, nine settlement labels, no in-boundary railway station and four Dutch NWB border links are internally coherent; neighbourhood population differs by nine residents (+0.072%) and is reconciled without rewriting CBS values. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Opmeer is a low, managed West-Frisian polder landscape whose Kaagpolder and other drainage units discharge through pumps, the VRNK/Raaksmaats boezem and wider Vier Noorder Koggen system; the municipality specifically identifies increasing pluvial risk at 't Wuiver in central Spanbroek. The canonical coastal case instead emits an exact 1.943328 floodDepthM field, 6,539 affected resident-equivalents and partial T+72 recovery without selecting an IJsselmeer/Amstelmeer boundary, Westfriese Omringdijk or regional-defence failure, boezem level, polder connection, breach, arrival or dewatering. The zero river preset is appropriate only as absence of a selected major-river pathway, never proof that regional-water flooding is impossible. A common neighbourhood seed repeats across pluvial, coastal, heat, winter and wildfire maps. A controlled fire in Braakpolder en Kolk van Dussen ranks its containing neighbourhood thirty-eighth of 46. Canonical wildfire is remote-smoke-only and omits grass/reed/crop fuel, wind, current regional fire phase, access, firewater and suppression. Static residents omit the approximately 9,000 visitors and livestock reported at the one-day 2026 Landbouwshow in De Weijver. Rural road and bus geometry do not establish event operation or access to external acute care; no acute-care department lies inside GM0432. Exact utility, water-chain, supply and recovery outputs lack physical topology, current state and accountable first-72-hour actions. Static plans, scenarios, current observations/alerts and synthetic results must remain explicitly distinct; Unknown and NoData are never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0432 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0432 as Opmeer in Noord-Holland and reports 12,491 residents, density 301/km2, 23.4% aged 65 or older and 1,905 one-person households. The generated centre [4.955083029916637, 52.71371212548708] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Forty-six neighbourhood rows in five districts sum to 12,500 residents, nine above the municipality total (+0.072%); households sum to 5,480 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 2,905. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 12,491 without altering source rows.

BAG supplies five current woonplaatsen—Aartswoud, De Weere, Hoogwoud, Opmeer and Spanbroek—and BRT supplies nine settlement labels: eight woonkernen and one deelkern. All place reference points are contained; labels are not occupancy, evacuation or service footprints.

Core population/age fields cover 46/46 neighbourhoods, but home-value/tenure fields cover 38/46 and cars per household 28/46; district heating and public charging cover 0/46. Published zero, null, suppression and not-applicable remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Programma Stedelijk Water en Riolering, Stedelijk Waterplan and Spanbroek water-overload priority
evidenceSources.edition: Stedelijk Waterplan 2024–2027 adopted 5 October 2023; Programma Stedelijk Water en Riolering 2022–2027 and Kadernota 2026–2029 pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality distinguishes duties for wastewater, rainwater and groundwater under its 2022–2027 programme from surface-water management; most urban surface-water management transferred to HHNK on 1 January 2023.

The adopted 2024–2027 plan covers municipal ditches, water bodies and bank protection, while HHNK monitors water quality and manages protection against flooding, water overload and shortage. Governance boundaries matter to first-72-hour actions.

The 2025 adopted framework says climate change creates growing water-overload risk in the centre of Spanbroek at 't Wuiver and links adaptation to sewer renewal and public-space redesign. This is planning evidence, not an event-time rainfall, depth, road or sewer state.

The deployment does not ingest the supported Wuiver footprint, sewer/groundwater response or owner/action state. No standard machine-readable reuse licence or live operational cadence was identified for the municipal plans/maps.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Vier Noorder Koggen, Kaagpolder and VRNK/Raaksmaats boezem system context
evidenceSources.edition: Current peilbesluit index and Vier Noorder Koggen decision/source document; Kaagpolder and Raaksmaatsboezem authority pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: HHNK's official Vier Noorder Koggen description divides the area into drainage units, inlets and target levels. The larger system ultimately pumps to the IJsselmeer, while water can be supplied near Opmeer from the Verenigde Raaksmaat- en Niedorperkoggeboezem.

Kaagpolder between Opmeer and Obdam is approximately 355 ha, historically marshy peat and dependent on pumped drainage to the Raaksmaatsboezem; the current electric pump and still-operable Kaagmolen illustrate managed drainage and backup potential.
The authority explains that high boezem levels can prevent polders from discharging and create water overload. This is a polder–pump–boezem–outfall chain, not direct centroid-to-coast propagation.

Peilbesluit design capacities and historic descriptions do not establish current pump availability, level, inlet/outlet state, power/backup, local connectivity, maintenance, failure, breach, emergency operation or T+72 recovery. Standard website reuse terms were not identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management / safety regions / water authorities
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Official Overstroomik scenario and uncertainty semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Current public explanation inspected 3 September 2026; interactive address map was temporarily unavailable during audit
supports: The official consortium says displayed water heights are based on selected representative extreme scenarios from the main and regional water systems and may be lower in a real event. Roads in an inundated area are assumed unavailable for evacuation in its public guidance.

The public explanation confirms that source system, scenario selection and maximum-height interpretation are essential metadata; it does not validate the simulator's canonical coastal amplitude, probability, footprint or timing.

The interactive address map returned temporarily unavailable during audit. Opmeer-specific cells could not be independently extracted from that interface and therefore remain NoData rather than zero or safe.
A decision-facing case needs an accessible, versioned LIWO/authority scenario with defence/breach, connected polder/boezem cells, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, uncertainty and licence.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regional risk, Opmeer fire-cover and current nature-fire phase context
evidenceSources.edition: Dekkingsplan and Beleidsplan 2024–2027; current nature-fire pages and homepage inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The regional plans identify Opmeer explicitly and treat flooding, extreme-weather, nature-fire, utilities, cyber, healthcare and transport pressures as regional concerns. A regional hazard family does not validate local amplitude or service curves.

The regional homepage still showed high nature-fire risk on 3 September 2026 following an August phase-2 notice. In phase 2, dry vegetation may support faster unpredictable spread and fire response uses more vehicles.

The authority says nature-fire operations depend on access, extinguishing water, escape routes/plans, location, wind/vegetation and current information. These are absent from the canonical and controlled Opmeer fire cases.

The dated phase is readiness context, not proof of a GM0432 ignition/perimeter or future valid state. Plans/alerts do not establish incident-time crew availability, arrival, containment or restoration; no blanket standard redistribution licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Calendar-bound Landbouwshow people, livestock, venue and heat-response context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal report published 3 August 2026; organizer event pages/results current for 3 August 2026 and inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality calls the annual first-Monday-of-August Landbouwshow at De Weijver Noord-Holland's largest agricultural event and says it attracts thousands of visitors, professionals, companies, families and livestock.

The primary organizer reports approximately 9,000 visitors for the 2026 edition, a roughly ten-hectare venue and a one-day 08:30–17:30 schedule; it also documents a heat protocol, drinking water, shade and an attending veterinarian.

CBS neighbourhood De Weijver contains only 25 published residents. Resident allocation therefore cannot represent event visitors, exhibitors, staff, responders, livestock, vehicles or their medical, water, shade, sanitation, traffic and evacuation needs.

Attendance is a dated event observation, not a permanent population. The organizer site supplies no standard open-data licence; any integration should use privacy-safe aggregate ranges and event-valid time.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Rural road, rail/transit and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light snapshot 1 August 2026 and ProRail/GTFS/RIVM snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: No ProRail station lies in GM0432; the deployment contains 34 GTFS stop areas. Stops/schedules do not establish event operation, passengers, accessibility, bus capacity, diversion or recovery.

The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph has four links over N239/N241 toward Medemblik, Hollands Kroon and Dijk en Waard. Same named corridor sections are series/non-additive and nominal 150 units are synthetic, not observed emergency throughput.

RIVM assigns no emergency department inside GM0432. Nearest straight-line reference points are Dijklander Hoorn at 9.967 km, Noordwest Alkmaar at 17.508 km and Dijklander Purmerend at 23.693 km; CC0 register roles and distance are not travel time, acceptance, staffing, beds or capacity.

Rural villages, external hospitals and an event venue require destination- and time-aware routes, local-road/bridge/passability state and alternatives; no matched in-boundary NDW situation is never proof that roads are open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / HHNK / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / RWS Waterinfo / NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial public water assets, current drought, grid, communications, education and observation context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HHNK drought liveblog updated 26 August 2026 and inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 151 GM0432 points: two sewer pumps, 29 surface-water pumps, three sluices and 117 weirs. Capacity exists for both sewer pumps and 27 surface pumps, not the sluices/weirs; connectivity, compatible units, current settings, operation, reserve, backup and restoration remain unavailable.

HHNK's 26 August drought update says no general irrigation ban was introduced, lake levels were low but stable, current measures were sufficient and water use should remain economical. It is regional timestamped state, not local groundwater, drinking-water or future availability.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Liander area OS DE WEEL 20-1i and contains null existing/required capacities plus queues/projects. RDI has 29 antenna installations (five mobile, eight fixed-link, sixteen amateur); DUO has six primary-school records. These are planning/register context, not live topology, outage, backhaul, shelter, occupancy or restoration.

No RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast, KNMI weather station or NDW road situation is assigned inside GM0432. Nearest reviewed KNMI observation is Berkhout at 8.047 km and Waterinfo level is Krabbersgat at 22.033 km. Bounded absence is NoData, never normal weather/water or open roads. Licences/cadences remain source-specific.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services with finite deterministic output.
notes: The mandatory municipality gate covers storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, earthquake, wildfire and compound for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Peak severity / maximum checkpoint affected resident-equivalents / T+72 event-attributable person-hours are: storm 0.495198 / 1,143 / 102,605.314; pluvial 0.542430 / 2,064 / 138,428.407; river 0 / 0 / 0; coastal 0.594200 / 6,539 / 445,350.560; heat 0.512272 / 359 / 77,318.516.

Affected population is a modelled resident-equivalent threshold, not observed people, casualties, evacuees, event visitors or patients. Wildfire can show zero affected while accumulating service-burden person-hours; both remain synthetic metrics.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation and cumulative burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0432 pnpm audit:model passed both tests over the complete matrix.
Service availability remains in [0,1]; hazard, demand, delivery, affected residents and burden remain finite/non-negative; repeated runs are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.
All 46 neighbourhoods allocate and reconcile exactly to 12,491 residents for every service; local demand/delivery closes to municipality totals and selected display layer does not change hazard.
Passing arithmetic does not establish polder/boezem hydraulics, drainage, defence failure, fire spread, transient presence, rural access, physical lifeline topology or restoration calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic coastal proximity and a shared neighbourhood seed override Opmeer's polder, drainage, fire-source and event geography.
notes: Coastal T+24 emits exactly 1.943328 in floodDepthM without selecting IJsselmeer/Amstelmeer boundary, Westfriese Omringdijk or regional-defence failure, boezem/polder connection, breach, arrival, duration, recession or dewatering.

At T+24 pluvial, coastal, heat, winter and wildfire all rank Spanbroek Centrum, Tussen Van Catz en Stolp, Slothuis, Schoolstraat, Planetenbuurt, Pastoor Merius, Weidebloem Oost and Zuiderzeebuurt first in essentially the same order.

A controlled T+24 fire source at the centre of Braakpolder en Kolk van Dussen produces direct fire 0.456625, smoke 0.477598 and 2,404 affected resident-equivalents, yet its containing neighbourhood ranks thirty-eighth of 46 with only eight affected residents.

Administrative centroids and a deterministic seed cannot replace hydraulic cells/levels/controls, rain and drainage flow paths, eligible grass/reed/crop fuel, source/wind/fire spread or venue-time people/animal geometry.

One Liander planning sample and 29 antennas cannot calibrate electricity/gas/telecom topology, current load, outage, backhaul, reserve, switching or restoration; six schools are not shelters/occupied facilities by default.

notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure contributions reconcile exactly.

KNMI/Waterinfo/NDW observations, HWH/NBNL/RDI/DUO/RIVM registers, current alerts and official plans correctly remain affectsSimulation=false; dated evidence must not silently drive an unbound exercise.

The trace does not select a defence/breach/polder case, Wuiver rain/drainage response, fire source/fuels/weather, Landbouwshow presence, cyber target, route condition, care destination or physical service network.
First-72-hour actions lack authority/owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, prerequisite, execution, verification, expiry and rollback states.

recovery72h.summary: Generic coastal recovery and persistent compound impacts have no local water-control, access, event, utility, fire or care evidence.
notes: At T+72 coastal still has 1,896 affected resident-equivalents, Facilities 0.709702 and 445,350.560 person-hours; no selected defence, pumping, warning, evacuation, dewatering, route, inspection, repair or resupply sequence explains the partial recovery.

Real polder response depends on level, pump/sluice/weir and power state plus decisions and access; 72 hours is neither automatic recovery nor an all-clear.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, geography and resident totals reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM0432, Opmeer, Noord-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Noord-Holland-Noord agree; the centre and five BAG place points are contained. CBS reports 12,491 residents while 46 neighbourhood rows total 12,500 (+0.072%).
findings.action: Retain authoritative code/name/boundary and source values, the nine-person reconciliation difference, field-level null semantics, editions and licences. Do not rewrite rounded observations.

findings.summary: The coastal preset selects no defence, boezem or polder pathway but emits decision-facing flood precision.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 reports floodDepthM 1.943328 and 6,539 affected resident-equivalents without an IJsselmeer/Amstelmeer boundary, Westfriese Omringdijk/regional-defence failure, boezem level, pump state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Official evidence describes a managed polder–boezem–outfall system and representative scenarios, not generic coast distance.
findings.action: Suppress depth, exposure and local ranks until an expert-selected versioned HHNK/RWS/LIWO case states source water, defence/breach, connected cells, datum, timing and uncertainty. Keep river zero as no selected major-river pathway, not a general flood-safe label.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial output does not encode Wuiver or managed polder/boezem drainage.
findings.evidence: Pluvial peaks at severity 0.542430 with 2,064 affected resident-equivalents and repeats the coastal neighbourhood order. The municipality specifically flags increasing water-overload risk at 't Wuiver in central Spanbroek; HHNK evidence shows pumping, target levels and boezem discharge determine outcomes. Neither footprint nor operational control is ingested.
findings.action: Integrate a licensed/versioned municipal or national stress-test footprint with rainfall duration, surface flow/elevation, buildings/roads and reviewed aggregate sewer/polder/boezem response. Keep depth, passability and drainage Unknown where hydraulic support/state is absent.

findings.summary: Unrelated hazards reuse a precise 46-neighbourhood ordering that overrides source geography.
findings.evidence: Pluvial, coastal, heat, winter and wildfire share essentially the same leaders. A focused Braakpolder/Kolk van Dussen fire source ranks its containing cell 38th, with eight affected residents, while distant urban cells rank first. This ordering is deterministic seed/proximity, not mechanism support.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific official/transparent support and add source-containment, hydraulic-connectivity and cross-hazard-rank-independence regressions. Unsupported rankings render Unknown.

findings.summary: Canonical wildfire and a rural source do not represent Opmeer grass/reed/crop fire operations.
findings.evidence: Canonical T+24 wildfire is remote-smoke-only: direct fire zero, smoke 0.259652 and zero threshold-affected residents despite 56,126.499 T+72 person-hours. The controlled rural source yields direct fire 0.456625 and 2,404 affected but ranks its source cell 38th. Current regional phase 2 establishes readiness, not source, fuels, wind, perimeter, access, firewater or suppression.
findings.action: Create separately named rural grass/reed/crop-fire and external-smoke cases with explicit source/perimeter, eligible fuel, event-valid wind/moisture, farms/people/animals, access/firewater, warning/closure and suppression state. Refresh phase evidence by exercise time.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure misses Landbouwshow visitors, livestock and operational demand at De Weijver.
findings.evidence: The model reconciles only 12,491 residents, including 25 in neighbourhood De Weijver. The organizer reports about 9,000 visitors on 3 August 2026 at a ten-hectare venue with livestock, parking, drinking water, shade, veterinarian and a heat protocol; none changes demand, exposure or actions.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe calendar-bound visitors, exhibitors, staff, responders, livestock and vehicle ranges plus venue ingress/egress, medical/veterinary, shade, drinking-water, sanitation, shelter and evacuation resources. Never apply them outside event validity.

findings.summary: The logical graph does not establish rural, event, bus or external acute-care access.
findings.evidence: Four N239/N241 links connect only three neighbouring municipalities and use nominal units; same-corridor sections are series. No station lies inside GM0432 and 34 GTFS stops lack operation/capacity. No acute-care department lies in Opmeer; Dijklander Hoorn is 9.967 km straight-line away, not an incident-time route or acceptance state.
findings.action: Model local rural/bridge/event and multi-hop ambulance routes, bus alternatives and care destinations with direction, restriction, capacity, destination acceptance/diversion and valid time. Missing operation or route state is Unknown, not open.

findings.summary: Exact eight-service percentages have no validated physical water or utility topology and current state.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 emits exact availability from Drainage 0.226811 and Power 0.350618 to Supply 0.849161. The 151 HWH points, one Liander sample, 29 antennas, six schools, road edges and external care provide context but not connected water/sewer/power/gas/telecom, facility, shelter, supply, backup, crew or repair state.
findings.action: Keep registers affectsSimulation=false and replace operator-looking decimals with evidence-backed ranges/zones or Unknown. Integrate only safe authorized aggregate dependencies with topology scope, valid time, uncertainty and restoration; do not reconstruct sensitive infrastructure.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration and recovery are not driven by accountable water, access, event, fire, care or utility actions.
findings.evidence: Coastal partially recovers to 1,896 affected and Facilities 0.709702 at T+72 without a defence/pump/dewatering ledger; compound remains 7,509 affected with Drainage 0.219631. Wildfire smoke clears without containment evidence. No owner/resource/action timeline exists.
findings.action: Require T+0/6/12/24/48/72 incident, decision, action and resource records with authority/owner, trigger, target, prerequisite, route, people/crew/material/stock, start/end, state, evidence/valid time, uncertainty and rollback. Only confirmed actions change trajectories.

findings.summary: Plans, representative flood cases, current alerts/observations, event reports, registers and synthetic outputs need explicit separation.
findings.evidence: The UI can juxtapose a water plan, unavailable Overstroomik address map, current drought/fire status, external weather/water points, an observed one-day event and exact synthetic T+72 values. None alone establishes a local incident, route, pump, outage, hospital or recovery state.
findings.action: Attach publisher, dataset/version, retrieval, issue/observation/valid/exercise time, evidence class, licence, spatial support, coverage, uncertainty, affectsSimulation and NoData to every map/card/export. Missing in-boundary data and inaccessible maps never become zero or safe.

residualLimitations: No expert-selected HHNK/RWS/LIWO scenario supplies an IJsselmeer/Amstelmeer boundary, Westfriese Omringdijk/regional-defence state, breach/overtopping, connected polder/boezem footprint, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, recession and dewatering for GM0432.

The municipal Wuiver concern is authoritative planning evidence, but the deployment lacks a licensed stress-test cell/road/building footprint, rainfall duration, surface flow, sewer/groundwater state, uncertainty and update metadata.
